thread.title: Fox bets $100 million on Redwood City-based Twitch rival

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Fox bets $100 million on Redwood City-based Twitch rival
text: Sep 6, 2018, 7:26am PDT Updated Sep 6, 2018, 7:29am PDT Looking ahead to its business post-Disney acquisition, 21st Century Fox has invested $100 million in Caffeine, a next-generation social broadcast platform for gaming, entertainment and other creative content. The investment is part of a larger round in which existing investors Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock Partners and others participated, though only Fox’s share was disclosed. In addition, Caffeine announced a content agreement with Live Nation (NYSE: LYV) to bring live music concerts to its platform starting in the fourth quarter. Fox (NASDAQ: FOXA, FOX) invested a combined $100 million in Caffeine and a newly formed venture called Caffeine Studios that is jointly owned by both companies. The new studio will produce exclusive esports, video game, sports and live entertainment content for Caffeine’s platform. In addition, Fox Executive Chairman Lachlan Murdoch will join Caffeine's board. Fox’s investments in Caffeine and Caffeine Studios will be part of the new Fox that will be formed after The Walt Disney Co. (NYSE: DIS) completes its acquisition of Fox’s entertainment assets. "The combination of the Caffeine platform with a content studio that benefits from Fox Sports' expertise in live events and programming will help position Caffeine to deliver compelling experiences in esports, video gaming and entertainment," Murdoch said in a statement . Founded in 2016 by former Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) executives Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, Caffeine previously raised $46 million over two rounds from Silicon Valley venture-capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Greylock Partners. The Bay Area venture aims to differentiate itself from live-streaming platforms such as Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN)-owned Twitch and Google’s YouTube (NASDAQ: GOOGL, GOOG) by prioritizing discovery and conversations on the platform from friends — a move that also aspires to limit “toxic chatter and endless feeds of meaningless comments.” The platform also offers an ad-free monetization system through viewer purchases of digital items that enhance the content experience while generating money for broadcasters. "We want to bring the world together around friends and live broadcasts," added Caffeine CEO Keighran. "It's an ambitious goal, but one we believe is attainable with the support of our amazing new partners, our awesome and ever-growing community, and the content that together, we can bring onto the platform." Caffeine is currently in pre-release.
